# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 94 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 94 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_094_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 11

**1** "First learn who I am," he said to me. I said to him, "Lord, teach me." "Who do you think the tall man is, the one who has the name of the Son of God?" he asked me. **2** "I said to him, "The Son of God is the man who was clothed in the Holy Spirit of God." "You said rightly," he answered; "for the Son of God is the one clothed in the Holy Spirit, **3** and through him the whole world was created and sustained. And see also: he is more ancient than all creation, and through him God laid the foundation of all things. He is the foundation and the cornerstone." **4** "But why then," I asked, "does he sometimes appear as old and other times as young?" "He appeared as ancient," he answered, "because the Son of God is pre-existent and appeared to his servants before and after; he appeared as ancient to those of the old covenant, but to those of the new he appeared as young and new. **5** And what you see is the new age; for he renews all things and makes them new. **6** But the old things were done and have passed away. And he chose twelve people and gave them power, that they should walk in his commandments. But after them he appointed twelve more, and then seven. All of these walked in the power of the Son of God."

---

*EMET: this chapter contains the Shepherd's most developed christology. The Son of God as pre-existent, as foundation and cornerstone, as the one in whom the Holy Spirit is clothed — this is subordinationist but high christology for c. 150 CE.*
